action.Q1A.001: He’s lost his ball. The red one dropped by the pond. He looked for it with his eyes for a bit, then delegated the job to me.
action.Q1A.002: I’ll keep an eye out for it. But I’m not going in the water.
action.Q1A.003: You don’t have to. It stayed on the dry side of the railing.
action.Q1A.x02: I did the searching, he did the leading. To every other dog in the village.
action.Q1A.x03: By the retention pond in Čierna Voda, where the cycle path ends.
action.Q1A.x04: If I find it, Bodka will owe me one.
action.Q1A.x05: Bodka owes nobody anything. But he’ll lick your shoe.
action.Q1A.journal: Lenka says Bodka lost his ball by the retention pond.
action.Q1B.label: Take the red ball
action.Q1B.001: Dry and thoroughly chewed. The owner will come forward himself.
action.Q1B.journal: I have Bodka’s ball. I’ll give it back to Lenka.
action.Q1C.label: Give Bodka his ball back
action.Q1C.001: One ball, found. Signed with teeth.
action.Q1C.x01: Now he’ll lose it again. But at least we know where.
action.Q1C.x02: Next time write your phone number on it.
action.Q1C.journal: Bodka has his ball back. He said thank you, briefly.
action.Q2A.001: If you’d be so kind, young man. I only need the pick-up hours. I’m not starting a whole new digital life for them.
action.Q2A.002: I’ll ask Ela for a notice in large print. On paper.
action.Q2A.003: Then thank you in advance. In capital letters.
action.Q2A.x01: The hours are in that QR code. You just point your phone at it.
action.Q2A.x02: I pointed my magnifying glass at it. It showed me the same little square, only bigger.
action.Q2A.x03: And put the phone number on it too. I can talk into a telephone. I can’t talk into a square.
action.Q2A.journal: Mr Jozef needs the pick-up hours in large print. I’ll ask Ela for a big notice.
action.Q2B.001: I have. Neighbourhood help, the hours and the phone number, all in large print. And no QR code.
action.Q2B.002: Mr Jozef will be able to read the big one from the bench.
action.Q2B.x02: I’ve got three versions. A small one for young people, a medium one for the noticeboard and a big one for Mr Jozef.
action.Q2B.x03: Just pin it up the right way round. Someone once put it up upside down and people rang numbers that don’t exist.
action.Q2B.journal: Ela gave me a large-print notice. I’ll pin it to the noticeboard in Čierna Voda.
action.Q2C.label: Pin the large notice to the noticeboard
action.Q2C.002: Even the phone number is in large print.
action.Q2C.003: There you are. Today technology has advanced by one sheet of paper.
action.Q2C.x01: There. Four drawing pins, so the wind doesn’t blow it away before you’ve read it.
action.Q2C.x02: And I didn’t even have to unfold my magnifying glass. I’ll save it for the crosswords.
action.Q2C.x03: Thank you kindly, young man. I could read this from the bus.
action.Q2C.journal: The notice is on the noticeboard. Mr Jozef can read it without his magnifying glass.
action.Q9E.001: Not every child has a computer of their own at home. With the club, we repair old laptops. They’re not new, but they work.
action.Q9E.002: And it all started with that one schematic?
action.Q9E.003: And with someone letting me explain it.
action.Q9E.x02: Me and twelve children. I say where the fault is, and the children pretend they knew.
action.Q9E.x04: No need. I think they know.
action.Q9E.journal: Jana and her club repair old laptops for children who don’t have a computer at home.
entry.S01.001: My garage. I’ve been fixing the neighbour’s radio since September. It already picks up one station, as long as I don’t breathe near it.
look.S01.ambient 1: Unsorted screws. I’ll sort them. I’ve been saying that for three years.
look.S01.ambient 2: The radio picks up hiss and one station that isn’t far off hiss.
look.S01.fuse: Spare fuses for small devices. Which one I need, I’ll only find out from the broken one.
look.S01.tools: My tool bag: a screwdriver with bits, pliers and a multimeter. I never leave the house without it.
entry.S02.001: Our lane. Every fence different, a different dog behind each one, and they all know me by my footsteps.
look.S02.LENKA: Lenka is holding the lead. Bodka is convinced she needn’t bother.
look.S02.ROMAN: Roman, the courier. He can deliver a parcel from a description of the gate.
look.S02.ambient 1: A ceramic owl guarding exactly seven centimetres of fence.
look.S02.ambient 2: The sticker says no junk mail. Three flyers are sticking out from under it.
entry.S03.001: Lúčny koník. The wooden grasshopper in the playground watches Ela under the shelter, handling phone calls and potatoes at the same time.
look.S03.ELA: Ela has a list for everything except a break.
look.S03.ambient 1: Tape on the ground marks two metres’ distance. Ela has paced them out; I’d manage about one metre eighty.
look.S03.ambient 2: Ela’s flask says DO NOT TOP UP WITH SOUP. That’ll be from experience.
look.S03.supplies: For every bag Ela has the recipient’s name and consent. She writes in pencil – the orders change until the last minute.
entry.S04.001: The shop at the hatch. Dana passes bags through it faster than I can say good morning.
look.S04.DANA: Dana can tell a customer by their shopping, even through a mask.
look.S04.ambient 1: Handwritten prices, all round sums. Small change is awkward to pass through a hatch.
look.S04.ambient 2: A few potatoes are already sprouting. Another week and Dana will be selling them as seed potatoes.
entry.S05.001: Gran’s gate. Gran is in quarantine, so today I’m not allowed any further than the little table.
look.S05.ambient 1: Gran knows the names of all the varieties and all the neighbours. She’s more forgiving with the varieties.
look.S05.ambient 2: The WELCOME mat is turned with the lettering towards the door. Since March it only welcomes people who are leaving.
look.S05.shed_door: Gran’s workshop stands in the garden, separate from the house. Gran’s key opens the lock on the door.
look.S05.tray: This is where I leave the shopping. Gran will only take it once I’ve stepped back.
exit.S05.to_S06.locked: First I’ll put Gran’s shopping on the table. Then I’ll go to the window.
exit.S05.to_S09.locked: The workshop door is locked. I’ll have to unlock it with Gran’s key first.
conn.S05.S06.locked: First I’ll put Gran’s shopping on the table. Then I’ll go to the window.
conn.S05.S09.locked: The workshop door is locked. I’ll have to unlock it with Gran’s key first.
entry.S06.001: Gran’s window. She’s behind the glass, I’m below it, and there’s a phone between us. That’s how visiting works round here now.
look.S06.MIRA20: Gran. Even from a closed room she has a firmer grip on the situation than I do.
look.S06.ambient 1: Gran calls it ‘the Engineer’. It has survived every one of her experiments.
look.S06.ambient 2: I remember this net curtain from when I was little. So far it looks as if it remembers me too.
look.S06.photo: Gran, me and a crooked horizon. I took it, and it shows.
look.S06.photo.variant1: Gran’s name and her outline are fading from the photo. The chronometer protects my memory, not the photo behind the window.
look.S06.photo.variant2: Gran’s name is readable again; her outline is still pale. The cause must be somewhere in the future.
look.S06.photo.variant3: The whole family is back. The crooked horizon too. I wouldn’t fix that one today.
exit.S06.to_S05.locked: First I’ll put Gran’s shopping on the table. Then I’ll go to the window.
entry.S09.001: Gran calls this ‘a few things’. A storeman would call it ‘a small warehouse’.
look.S09.ambient 1: Three skis. Gran knows exactly why three, and it’ll be perfectly logical.
look.S09.ambient 2: A school globe. Half the countries on it don’t exist any more, but the oceans are spot on.
look.S09.case: A brass case with ZVON and the name M. Hrušková on it. It isn’t locked; it just looks important.
exit.S09.to_S05.locked: The workshop door is locked. I’ll have to unlock it with Gran’s key first.
entry.S10.001: There’s a warning on the wall: DO NOT OVERWRITE THE ORIGINAL. The one I know is DO NOT OPEN. I never obeyed that one.
look.S10.ambient 1: Four pencils, three eras, one dried-up marker.
look.S10.ambient 2: DO NOT OVERWRITE THE ORIGINAL, underlined three times. Gran doesn’t underline anything she doesn’t mean.
look.S10.chrono: A base node with a low-voltage cradle. The portable part goes in the middle. When the cradle doesn’t light up, it’s the fuse.
look.S10.panel: The diagram above the panel connects circle to circle, triangle to triangle and square to square. The colour doesn’t matter.
entry.S51.001: The Dúbravka stop. I used to go to school from here, and the waiting is still exactly the same.
look.S51.ambient 1: The same chipped corner of the kerb. I tripped over it all through my first years at school.
look.S51.ambient 2: It shows how many minutes until the bus comes. Today I’d appreciate the year as well.
look.S51.clock: When they rebuilt the stop, they kept the original brass clock frame. It was already hanging here when I went to school.
exit.S51.to_S07.label: Bus to Čierna Voda
travel.S51.to_S07.first.001: Back to Čierna Voda. From there I could find my way to Grob blindfolded.
entry.S52.001: My old school. The first time I’ve ever heard it completely silent.
look.S52.ambient 1: A notice: classrooms closed to visitors, items handed out by permit only. I stood up straighter at once.
look.S52.ambient 2: The same flowerpot by the gate. There was no flower in it in my day either, just chewing gum wrappers.
look.S52.photo: From the pavement I can see the corner of the yard and the service window with the metal swallow. The yard is all tarmac – no tree, no low wall.
exit.S52.to_S53.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
exit.S52.to_S55.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
conn.S52.S53.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
conn.S52.S55.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
entry.S56.001: Tóno, our caretaker. When he unlocked the prep room for me in 1995, he didn’t have grey temples yet.
look.S56.TONO20: Fifty-year-old Tóno at the same window. He’s turning a small key in his fingers, just like in 1995.
look.S56.ambient 1: Tóno has the same metal swallow on the ledge. A bit battered, but holding on.
look.S56.ambient 2: Tóno is mending a birdhouse for the school yard. Even in a closed school, someone is thinking about the children coming back.
entry.S53.001: When I came to school here, they wouldn’t let me in without indoor shoes. Today it’s without a mask and hand gel.
look.S53.ambient 1: Perspex with a little hatch for papers. You can say hello, but you can’t shake hands.
look.S53.ambient 2: Equipment to borrow at home. For now, the school fits into a box.
exit.S53.to_S52.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
exit.S53.to_S54.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
conn.S53.S54.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
entry.S54.001: The first time I’m in the prep room with permission and no fear of a bad mark. It only took me a quarter of a century.
look.S54.JANA20: Jana is on a video call on the laptop on the bench. She looks at me slightly from above, the way teachers used to from behind their desks.
look.S54.ambient 1: The same cupboard after all these years. I could find the scuff by the left hinge with my eyes closed.
look.S54.ambient 2: A loan laptop. A child’s name on the sticker, and underneath in pencil: ‘Homework first, then games.’
look.S54.log: The record of 7 December 1982: Oto’s drawing of the return bridge; his grandson Tóno helped. The bridge was lost later.
exit.S54.to_S53.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
entry.S55.001: I know this corner. I have a feeling something’s missing here, and it isn’t the bench.
look.S55.ambient 1: Distance markings on the tarmac for collections. While you wait, there’s no shade to hide in and nowhere to sit.
look.S55.ambient 1.variant1: The pick-up point is now under a big lime tree. The distance markings are still there, but now they’re in the shade.
look.S55.ambient 2: The same bin as in my day. The head teachers changed; the bin stayed.
look.S55.cache: There’s a low wall under the lime tree, but on my photo there’s only tarmac here. I’ll open the service board with the tools from my bag.
exit.S55.to_S52.locked: I’m only allowed into the school with a permit. First I’ll report to Tóno at the service window.
entry.S08.001: The pond below the pump track. Children ride up on the hill, ducks swim down below, and both lots make exactly the same noise.
look.S08.ambient 1: A duck. It has kept its distance from the bank ever since Bodka started coming here.
look.S08.ambient 2: I could sit here for a while and not save anything.
look.S08.ball: A chewed ball is lying on the dry side of the railing. Its canine owner doesn’t read lost-and-found notices.
entry.S07.001: There’s a QR code on the noticeboard and an old gentleman with a magnifying glass below it. Looks like they’ll need an interpreter.
look.S07.JOZEF: Mr Jozef with his folding magnifying glass. He can read everything on the noticeboard except the QR code.
look.S07.ambient 1: A ballroom dancing course. For the time being, everyone dances alone.
look.S07.ambient 2: Mr Jozef’s magnifying glass. Folding, in a leather case, no battery. I’d love to repair one like that, but there’s nothing to repair.
look.S07.board: The neighbourhood help hours are hidden in a tiny QR code. Ordinary letters would help more here.
look.S07.board.variant1: Large print, readable hours and the neighbourhood help contact. At last Mr Jozef doesn’t need his magnifying glass.
exit.S07.to_S51.label: Bus to Dúbravka
travel.S07.to_S51.first.001: By bus into town, then change for Dúbravka. Mask – check. Ticket – check.
travel.S07.to_S51.first.002: The bus is almost empty. Everyone sits at their own window, as if they’d booked it.
conn.S07.S51.label: Bus Čierna Voda – Dúbravka
topic.DANA.ambient 1.label: How’s business?
topic.DANA.ambient 1.001: What are you running out of fastest at the moment?
topic.DANA.ambient 1.002: Patience. And I’ve no way of reordering that.
topic.DANA.ambient 1.003: If a delivery does turn up, put two packs aside for me.
topic.DANA.ambient 1.x01: One. Your gran has already ordered the other.
topic.DANA.ambient 1.x02: Gran? She’s got enough patience for three.
topic.DANA.ambient 1.x03: Because she’s saving it for you.
topic.DANA.ambient 2.label: What did Gran order?
topic.DANA.ambient 2.001: The usual: tea and potatoes. And she says you’re not to carry the bag by one handle.
topic.DANA.ambient 2.002: Gran can even steer me through the shopkeeper.
topic.DANA.ambient 2.x01: Through the shopkeeper, through Ela and through the courier. She’s rung me twice today.
topic.DANA.ambient 2.x03: The second time she asked whether I remembered what she’d said the first time.
topic.DANA.extra 1.label: Regulars
topic.DANA.extra 1.001: Do you know people by their shopping?
topic.DANA.extra 1.002: By their shopping and by their walk. Mr Jozef walks slowly and shops fast: bread and the paper.
topic.DANA.extra 1.004: Nothing. Your gran does your shopping.
topic.DANA.extra 1.005: I bought myself some chocolate the other day.
topic.DANA.extra 1.006: I know. Your gran rang me afterwards to ask whether you’d had your lunch as well.
topic.DANA.extra 2.label: Selling through the hatch
topic.DANA.extra 2.001: How do you like selling through the hatch?
topic.DANA.extra 2.002: People argue less. Through glass it doesn’t have the same effect.
topic.DANA.extra 2.003: And what do you miss most?
topic.DANA.extra 2.004: Gossip. Only the quick kind fits through a hatch.
topic.DANA.extra 2.006: No. Quick gossip is just news. For proper gossip you need a bench.
topic.DANA.extra 3.label: Quarantine shopping
topic.DANA.extra 3.001: What are people buying most in quarantine?
topic.DANA.extra 3.002: Flour and yeast. The whole village has suddenly started baking.
topic.DANA.extra 3.004: Judging by how much bread they buy from me at the same time, not well so far.
topic.ELA.ambient 1.label: How are you coping?
topic.ELA.ambient 1.001: How many people need help today?
topic.ELA.ambient 1.002: More than yesterday. But there are more helpers too.
topic.ELA.ambient 1.003: Then put me down as a helper.
topic.ELA.ambient 1.x01: You’re already down. Gran signed you up this morning, with a note: ‘willing, but late’.
topic.ELA.ambient 1.x02: Late? I got here at ten.
topic.ELA.ambient 1.x03: She was expecting you at nine. That’s on the list too.
topic.ELA.ambient 2.label: That flask?
topic.ELA.ambient 2.001: Don’t top up with soup? Did that really happen here?
topic.ELA.ambient 2.002: Once. Someone topped up my coffee flask with soup from the pick-up. Once was enough.
topic.ELA.ambient 2.x02: The first sip. It was good soup, just bad coffee.
topic.ELA.ambient 2.x03: And who did that to you?
topic.ELA.ambient 2.x04: I’m not saying. I don’t give out personal data, not even about soup.
topic.ELA.extra 1.label: Volunteers
topic.ELA.extra 1.002: Two students, a teacher, and Roman when he’s passing.
topic.ELA.extra 1.003: A teacher, on top of remote learning?
topic.ELA.extra 1.004: Mornings she teaches over the camera, afternoons she packs bags here. She says at least potatoes don’t switch their cameras off.
topic.ELA.extra 1.006: Nobody. I just know who’s where and when. So everyone asks me anyway.
topic.ELA.extra 3.label: Lists
topic.ELA.extra 3.001: How many lists have you actually got?
topic.ELA.extra 3.002: Four. Shopping, medicines, phone numbers and a list of lists.
topic.ELA.extra 3.003: And what’s the fourth one for?
topic.ELA.extra 3.004: So I know which of the other three I can’t find right now.
topic.ELA.extra 3.006: She did. And she suggested a fifth: people who don’t answer the phone. You’re top of it.
topic.ELA.extra 2.label: Your daughter
topic.ELA.extra 2.001: How’s the little one? Well, probably not so little any more.
topic.ELA.extra 2.002: Nina? She stopped being little ages ago – she’s fifteen and doing school on the computer. She claims she’s studying. I can hear her laughing.
topic.ELA.extra 2.003: Maybe the teacher has left the microphone on and doesn’t know.
topic.ELA.extra 2.004: Maybe. In the evenings she helps me type the lists into the computer. She says one day she’ll have everything in one place.
topic.ELA.extra 2.005: Everything in one place? That sounds like a big plan.
topic.ELA.extra 2.006: She’s fifteen. Let her plan; I’ll lend her the lists for now.
topic.JANA20.ambient 1.label: How does lending out equipment work?
topic.JANA20.ambient 1.001: By appointment, one at a time. Whoever collects equipment signs a receipt and doesn’t meet anyone.
topic.JANA20.ambient 1.002: Paperwork that actually helps. Then I suppose nothing goes missing any more.
topic.JANA20.ambient 1.x01: It does. But we once spent a month looking for a microscope, and now I know where every ruler is.
topic.JANA20.ambient 1.x02: Even the ones that don’t come back?
topic.JANA20.ambient 1.x03: Those especially. They get a red circle in the register.
topic.JANA20.extra 1.label: Remote learning
topic.JANA20.extra 1.001: How does teaching at a distance work?
topic.JANA20.extra 1.002: In bits. Maths works; PE is harder.
topic.JANA20.extra 1.004: The children jump around in their living rooms. The neighbours downstairs confirm it works.
topic.JANA20.extra 2.label: Tóno at school
topic.JANA20.extra 2.001: What was Tóno like as a classmate?
topic.JANA20.extra 2.002: He drew aeroplanes in every exercise book. Including mine, when I wasn’t looking.
topic.JANA20.extra 2.004: I corrected them. The wings were always at the wrong angle.
topic.JOZEF.ambient 1.label: What kind of phone do you have?
topic.JOZEF.ambient 1.002: That’s still a very good feature.
topic.JOZEF.ambient 1.x01: My grandson wanted to buy me one of those glass ones. I asked him where the buttons were.
topic.JOZEF.ambient 1.x03: Everywhere. So I kept the one that at least has them all in one place.
topic.JOZEF.ambient 2.label: Waiting for the bus?
topic.JOZEF.ambient 2.001: No. I’m waiting for someone to tell me what’s in that little square on the noticeboard.
